additional_verified_behavior: Deleted counterparties remain on historical B2B invoices with immutable party identity and a deleted-business marker; private books are removed, other businesses' documents and shared evidence retained, and new trade/authentication refused.
Auth/Lock contexts retain their identity across hot reload; provider misuse still fails explicitly.
Notifications and migration/export inspection reuse the request connection. A pool of one can produce a real Field notification and scoped export reads without a second checkout.
Temporary pool exhaustion returns sanitized HTTP503 and Retry-After; unexpected errors do not expose raw exception text.
NULL-owned financial/import rows are reported without assigning them to arbitrary business 2.
Settlement serialization preserves the original operator-name snapshot and removes the origin database's local operator id; the existing receiving-side owner binding remains authoritative.
All three removed repair exports were recovered from an ignored encrypted local evidence vault and matched their original bytes. No real financial repair was applied.
failure_history: Earlier incomplete/interrupted runs are not counted as passes. The immediately preceding complete Billing run had 2513 passed, 23 skipped and six failures; final acceptance above resolves all six.

Those six exposed a real unportable settlement operator id, a source-contract assertion predating durable control delivery, Phase3 fixtures without an owner, and obsolete signup phone expectations. The sync payload was corrected and fixtures updated to valid current contracts.
The first complete Field standalone run had two outdated assertions for the newly exposed merchant VPA and local mirror columns; corrected assertions retain identity and migration checks.
The first Field PostgreSQL driver stopped at collection because Billing Alembic prepended its legacy app.py path; the driver now restores Field package precedence.

The next Field PostgreSQL run had 116 passed, 38 failed and 11 fixture errors: the Windows cluster's inherited WIN1252 encoding rejected the route arrow, and read-only mirror fixtures omitted required Billing UIDs. Generated test databases now explicitly use UTF8, and external-schema fixture writes use Billing's complete models. A foreign-receipt fixture now refers to a valid foreign-owned invoice while retaining the cross-business exclusion assertion.
fixture_cleanup: Both audit-owned PostgreSQL clusters were stopped after their resolved scratch paths and fixture ports were checked. Private test fixture files remain ignored for inspection; no user database was stopped.
remaining_external_gates: Rotate the confirmed exposed Supabase password, update every dependent secret and verify old-credential revocation through the authorized provider process.
Reconcile the existing over-receipt invoice, multiple open shifts and 18 overfilled invoices in the supplied old deployment log from original documents and cash counts.

Live migration head e70b5d2a4c06 was subsequently applied and retried successfully; dedicated constrained HTTP/trade/admin configuration and protocol2 installed-client rollout remain separate deployment work.
Demonstrate a live restore drill, phone/PWA/GPS and physical printer acceptance, offline reconnect and the planned paid merchant pilot.
Publication and later approved external operations are recorded separately in DEPLOYMENT.md. No historical financial-data repair, live payment or message to another person was performed.
